title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Resigns Amid Spy and Affair Scandal

beats.narration: Nvidia co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang has resigned. The departure follows a widening scandal involving affairs and alleged ties to Chinese intelligence.
A public letter demanding his reinstatement has drawn more than 115,000 signatures. Signers include Elon Musk and other tech executives, according to TechCrunch.

visual.name: TechCrunch
visual.headline: Elon Musk, other tech execs sign petition calling on Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang

beats.narration: Huang stepped down on Thursday after confessing to an affair with a chip executive suspected by U.S. intelligence of being a Chinese spy.
Nvidia appointed CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO while it searches for a permanent replacement. The board also named Harvey Jones as its first board chair, according to The Verge.
The New York Times reported in late October that Huang appeared to be the target of a Chinese spy plot. The report centered on Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed.

visual.name: The Verge
visual.headline: An overview of Jensen Huang’s messy days

beats.narration: Some U.S. officials believed she was passing information to Beijing. Megaspeed now says Alice Huang left the company in August 2025 and holds no role there.

visual.name: The Verge
visual.headline: An overview of Jensen Huang’s messy days

beats.narration: The petition says its signers are concerned that Huang was removed without meaningful due process. It demands that the board bring him back while an independent investigation establishes the facts.
President Trump said he does not believe the affair threatened national security. He also doubted that Alice Huang is a spy, contradicting prior U.S. official findings.

visual.speaker: Donald Trump, U.S. President
visual.text: Nobody's proven that she's a spy. She may not be a spy.

beats.narration: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said the AI industry will be fine without Huang. He called Huang a hero with flaws and said he does not know enough to judge whether Huang should return.

visual.name: TechCrunch
visual.headline: Sam Altman on Nvidia without Jensen Huang: The industry will be ‘fine’

beats.narration: Nvidia accounts for roughly 80 percent of the AI GPU market. The company has also reported billions in AI investments and commitments.

Shares closed at 162 dollars and 85 cents on November 13. That is down from an October 6 high of 239 dollars and 24 cents, according to The Verge. The Verge also reported that shares dropped 14 percent since the resignation.
Nvidia has agreed to guarantee up to 105 billion dollars for OpenAI's Ohio data center project. This is one of many circular deals Nvidia has made to bankroll the AI boom.
Nvidia's planned acquisition of Hugging Face is valued at nearly 13 billion dollars, according to MIT Technology Review.

visual.label: Nvidia planned acquisition of Hugging Face

beats.narration: Lawmakers have begun investigations into alleged chip smuggling. Nvidia's quarterly earnings are expected soon, and the future of the company remains in flux.
Reports say Huang is assembling a war room of allies to lobby for a comeback. Not everyone believes he should return, and one ally called an affair with a subordinate a fireable offense.

visual.name: The Verge
visual.headline: Jensen Huang might be plotting a return and more of the latest Nvidia drama

beats.narration: One analyst says Nvidia's market share, chips, and ecosystem will not change with one person. He says the fallout could take years to play out.

visual.speaker: Stephen Straus, CEO of KUNGFU.AI
visual.text: None of that changes with one person.

beats.narration: The petition count is disputed. TechCrunch reported more than 115,000 signatures, while The Verge later reported over 150,000.
The future of Nvidia and the wider AI industry remains in flux as the story develops.

visual.name: The Verge
visual.headline: The Nvidia scandal isn’t slowing down

beats.narration: We will keep following this story.
